# Results — Study 438 (Triple-MA-Crossover) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The triple moving-average
"ribbon" timing rule: go long the S&P 500 when **fast > medium > slow** (SMA 5/20/50),
else move to cash. Raced against buy-and-hold and the simpler **two-MA** cross (SMA 5/50,
same fast/slow legs). Tested on **^GSPC daily price-only closes** (no dividends) — so the
timing-vs-hold race is run **excess-of-cash** (cash credited at a flat **3%** proxy). One
documented execution lag (signal on close of t, position held over t+1). One-way cost =
**5 bps × NAV**; the optional short leg pays borrow. The in-progress final bar (today) is
dropped so no partial day enters the stamped run. As-of **2026-06-23**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC | 1993-01-04 → 2026-06-23 | 8,425 | `498c2ee76497` |

> Price-only index (no dividends), so all Sharpes are **net, excess-of-cash**, labelled as
> such. No survivorship issue (single index series). No partial bar (today dropped).

## The three-way race — buy-and-hold vs two-MA vs three-MA

A long/flat timing rule sits in cash part-time, so the fair race is **excess-of-cash to
excess-of-cash**, and the decisive control is the **simpler version of the same idea** (the
two-MA cross), not just buy-and-hold.

| Arm | CAGR | Net excess Sharpe | Max drawdown | HAC *t* (excess mean) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Buy-and-hold** | **+8.76%** | **+0.293** | −56.78% | +1.93 |
| **Two-MA 5/50** | +4.94% | **+0.167** | −32.91% | +1.05 |
| **Three-MA 5/20/50** | +3.24% | **+0.022** | −23.11% | **+0.14** |

- **Three-MA vs buy-and-hold:** HAC Sharpe-difference *t* = **−2.10** — the triple rule is
  *reliably worse* than simply holding the index.
- **Three-MA vs two-MA:** HAC Sharpe-difference *t* = **−1.46** — the third "confirmation"
  MA's marginal contribution to risk-adjusted return is **negative**.
- **Own significance:** the three-MA excess mean comes in at HAC *t* = **+0.14** — there is
  no edge to speak of, far under the *t* ≥ 2 bar.
- **In-market fraction:** 47.8% (triple) vs 67.0% (dual). The triple rule's lower drawdown
  is **exposure reduction** (out of the market half the time), not timing skill.

## Config robustness — it's the idea, not the tuning

| fast/mid/slow | Three-MA Sharpe | Three-MA *t* | Two-MA Sharpe | BH Sharpe | *t*(triple − dual) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5/20/50 | +0.022 | +0.14 | +0.167 | +0.293 | −1.46 |
| 10/50/200 | +0.242 | +1.50 | +0.424 | +0.293 | −2.27 |
| 20/50/100 | +0.226 | +1.49 | +0.260 | +0.296 | −0.76 |
| 5/10/20 | −0.187 | −1.14 | +0.088 | +0.297 | −2.38 |

In **4/4** configs the three-MA rule's Sharpe is below the two-MA rule's, and its own *t*
never clears 2. The famous **10/50/200** ribbon loses to its two-MA twin at *t* = −2.27.

## Cost sensitivity — there is nothing to charge costs against

| One-way cost | Three-MA Sharpe | CAGR |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +0.093 | +3.87% |
| 5 bps | +0.022 | +3.24% |
| 10 bps | −0.050 | +2.61% |
| 25 bps | −0.263 | +0.75% |

Even **gross** (0 bps) the three-MA Sharpe (+0.093) is below both buy-and-hold (+0.293) and
the two-MA rule (+0.167); it turns negative by 10 bps. Cost is a sideshow — the edge was
never there to charge against.

## Permutation null

Re-running the exact triple rule on 2,000 circular-block (21-day) reshuffles of the return
series: observed Sharpe **+0.022**, **p = 0.57** (null mean +0.050, sd 0.168). The observed
Sharpe sits in the middle of the luck cloud — no genuine trend signal under the strategy.

## Synthetic positive control (faithful-engine / power)

Deterministic two-regime panel with a planted trend `edge` (the harness must not fake a
signal at edge 0, and must detect one when planted):

| Planted edge | Three-MA Sharpe | Three-MA *t* | BH Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 (random walk) | −0.171 | −1.01 | −0.168 |
| 2.0 (strong trend) | +0.926 | +5.04 | +0.585 |

With no planted trend the rule sits at *t* ≈ −1 (no false positive); with a strong planted
trend the *same* engine reaches *t* = +5.04. The machinery is faithful — so the flat
real-tape *t* = +0.14 is a genuine null.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Three-MA net excess Sharpe +0.022, HAC *t* = +0.14 (far under 2),
  block-permutation p = 0.57. Indistinguishable from noise.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Below buy-and-hold (+0.293) **and** the two-MA rule (+0.167)
  even at 0 bps; negative by 10 bps. The lower drawdown is exposure reduction (47.8%
  in-market), not timing. Not even FRAGILE.
- **"Three beats two"? — BUSTED.** HAC *t*(triple − dual) = −1.46, and triple loses to dual
  in 4/4 configs. The third moving average subtracts risk-adjusted return: more confirmation
  → more lag → less return.
